**Artemis II** (April 1–11, 2026) flew a crew of four on a [flyby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flyby_(spaceflight) "Flyby (spaceflight)") of the [Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon "Moon"). It was the first crewed flight of the [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")-led [Artemis program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artemis_program "Artemis program"), the only beyond [low Earth orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_Earth_orbit "Low Earth orbit") (LEO) since [Apollo 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_17 "Apollo 17") in 1972, and the only beyond LEO not part of the [Apollo program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_program "Apollo program"). It was also the first crewed flight of the [Space Launch System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Launch_System "Space Launch System") and of the [Orion spacecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orion_(spacecraft) "Orion (spacecraft)"), which the crew named ***Integrity***.

Earlier in March 2026, NASA announced that the upper-stage helium-flow problem, which had previously necessitated a rollback for repairs, had been fixed and was undergoing validation.[[62]](#cite_note-62) On March 12, after a [Flight Readiness Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_Readiness_Review "Flight Readiness Review") (FRR), NASA cleared Artemis II's rocket for an April launch following these repairs, with the review polling 'go' to proceed toward an April 1 launch attempt.

NASA stated that the team and hardware were ready.[[63]](#cite_note-63)[[64]](#cite_note-64) Seven two-hour launch windows were announced for April 1–6 and April 30, with the first launch window being on April 1, 2026.[[65]](#cite_note-65) On March 18, NASA announced that the Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft would be [rolled out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crawler-transporter "Crawler-transporter") the next day to Launch Pad 39B at the agency's [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center") in Florida.

Meanwhile, the Artemis II crew entered [quarantine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarantine "Quarantine") in Houston, Texas, to ensure they remained healthy ahead of the launch.[[66]](#cite_note-66) On March 20, after a delay due to high winds,[[67]](#cite_note-67) the SLS was rolled out from the VAB to launch pad 39B a second time.[[68]](#cite_note-68)
| Mission Specialist | [Jenni Gibbons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenni_Gibbons "Jenni Gibbons"), CSA |

Artemis II was crewed by four astronauts: commander [Reid Wiseman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reid_Wiseman "Reid Wiseman"), pilot [Victor Glover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Glover "Victor Glover"), and mission specialist [Christina Koch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christina_Koch "Christina Koch"), all from the [NASA Astronaut Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Corps "NASA Astronaut Corps"), along with mission specialist [Jeremy Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Hansen "Jeremy Hansen") from the [Canadian Astronaut Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Astronaut_Corps "Canadian Astronaut Corps").[[69]](#cite_note-Artemis_Crew-69) On November 22, 2023, [Jenni Gibbons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenni_Gibbons "Jenni Gibbons") was named as Hansen's backup,[[70]](#cite_note-70) and on July 3, 2024, [Andre Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Douglas "Andre Douglas") was named as the backup for the three NASA astronauts.[[71]](#cite_note-Space.com1-71) Glover became the first [person of color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Person_of_color "Person of color"), Koch the [first woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_in_space "Women in space"), Wiseman the oldest person, and Hansen the first non-American to travel around the Moon.
This mission was Hansen's first spaceflight.
Artemis II lifts off from Launch Complex 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on April 1, 2026

The crew arrived at Kennedy Space Center on March 27,[[85]](#cite_note-NASA-2026a-85) and the launch countdown began on March 30.[[86]](#cite_note-86) The mission launched aboard an SLS rocket on April 1 from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B at 22:35:12 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time") (6:35:12 p.m. [EDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Daylight_Time "Eastern Daylight Time"), local time at the launch site).[[6]](#cite_note-NASA_Launch_Time-6)[[87]](#cite_note-87) It was the first crewed launch from LC-39B since [STS-116](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-116 "STS-116") in 2006.
### Return flight

The remainder of the day included staggered off-duty periods for rest ahead of final return preparations.[[118]](#cite_note-118) The day concluded with a 15-second trajectory correction burn, the first of three that refined the path of the spacecraft toward Earth.[[8]](#cite_note-Grimm_&_Zakrzewski_2026-8)[[119]](#cite_note-:1-119)
They then attached an inflatable raft, known as a "front porch", to the side hatch, and conducted initial checks before crew egress.[[133]](#cite_note-CBS_splashdown-133)[[134]](#cite_note-134)
Crew members exited the capsule individually onto the raft, where they were fitted with hoisting gear and lifted into helicopters.

pages.title: SpaceX launches four people on NASA's Crew-11 mission to ISS : NPR
passages: **SpaceX launches four people on NASA's Crew-11 mission to ISS** **NASA and SpaceX's Crew-11 mission is made up of two U.S. astronauts, one from Japan and a Russian cosmonaut. They'll be aboard the International Space Station for six months conducting research.**
### [Space](https://www.npr.org/sections/space/)
By
![Crew-11 mission astronauts wave as they head to the launch pad at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Fla. on Friday.
From Left to right, Roscosmos cosmonaut Oleg Platonov, NASA astronaut Mike Fincke, NASA astronaut and mission commander Zena Cardman and JAXA astronaut Kimiya Yui.

The crew will live and work aboard the International Space Station for at least six months.](https://npr.brightspotcdn.com/dims3/default/strip/false/crop/3115x1908+0+0/resize/1100/quality/50/format/jpeg/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fnpr-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F0d%2F9a%2Fecb3cf1148c69770a24ee5e8759c%2Fgettyimages-2227269222.jpg)
Crew-11 mission astronauts wave as they head to the launch pad at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Fla. on Friday.
From Left to right, Roscosmos cosmonaut Oleg Platonov, NASA astronaut Mike Fincke, NASA astronaut and mission commander Zena Cardman and JAXA astronaut Kimiya Yui.
Gregg Newton/AFP via Getty Images

An international crew of four launched into orbit just before noon Friday from Florida on [NASA's Crew-11](https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-11/), a six-month mission to the [International Space Station](https://www.nasa.gov/international-space-station/).
### [Space](https://www.npr.org/sections/space/)
### [SpaceX wants to go to Mars. To get there, environmentalists say it's trashing Texas](https://www.npr.org/2024/10/10/nx-s1-5145776/spacex-texas-wetlands)

SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket roared to life on Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39-A, lofting the company's [Dragon capsule](https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/dragon) and crew on a nine-minute trip from the Earth's surface into orbit.
The capsule is carrying NASA astronauts Zena Cardman and Mike Fincke, along with Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency astronaut Kimiya Yui and Russian cosmonaut Oleg Platonov.
ET.
They'll also perform experiments to produce a "higher volume of human stem cells and general on-demand nutrients."
The Crew-11 mission marks the 12th time SpaceX is launching NASA astronauts to the ISS.

In 2020, the private company began [ferrying astronauts to the station](https://www.npr.org/2020/05/30/864514995/spacex-and-nasa-try-once-more-to-launch-astronauts) as part of the agency's Commercial Crew Program, ending a reliance on Russia for rides to the station after the [retirement of the Space Shuttle program](https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2011/07/21/138564226/atlantis-on-schedule-for-landing-in-florida) in 2011.

![A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket with the Crew Dragon capsule Endeavour carrying the Crew-11 mission lifts off from Launch Complex 39A at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Friday.](https://npr.brightspotcdn.com/dims3/default/strip/false/crop/7311x4874+0+0/resize/1100/quality/50/format/jpeg/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fnpr-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2Ffd%2F03%2Fe8ec512e40f5a939e03b05380549%2Fgettyimages-2227286913.jpg)

A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket with the Crew Dragon capsule Endeavour carrying the Crew-11 mission lifts off from Launch Complex 39A at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Friday. **Chandan Khanna/AFP via Getty Images** ****hide caption****
Chandan Khanna/AFP via Getty Images
The 37-year-old geobiologist was selected by NASA in 2017 to join the astronaut corps.
### [Space](https://www.npr.org/sections/space/)
### [How the U.S. became highly reliant on Elon Musk for access to space](https://www.npr.org/2025/06/07/nx-s1-5425266/spacex-musk-trump-starlink-starship)

Wilmore and Williams had arrived at the space station [in Boeing's Starliner capsule](https://www.npr.org/2024/06/05/nx-s1-4956024/boeing-starliner-launch-nasa-international-space-station) on the spacecraft's first human test flight in June 2024.

But [hardware issues](https://www.npr.org/2024/07/03/nx-s1-5026448/boeing-starliner-astronauts-space-station-return) uncovered during that mission prompted NASA to select [a new ride home](https://www.npr.org/2025/03/12/nx-s1-5324653/trump-space-musk-astronauts-international-space-station-nasa) for the crew — leaving the Starliner with [no one aboard](https://www.npr.org/2024/09/07/nx-s1-5103722/starliner-nasa-boeing-crew-space-station-lands) for its trip back to Earth.

NASA and SpaceX flew Crew-9 to the station with [two empty seats](https://www.npr.org/2024/09/28/nx-s1-5132090/spacex-nasa-crew-9-launch) for Wilmore and Williams to use [for their return](https://www.npr.org/2025/03/18/nx-s1-5331907/nasa-astronauts-return-long-space-station-suni-williams-butch-wilmore) in March.
But space flight is not about me or about any individual.
It's about what we can do together," said Cardman. "Now I have the opportunity to train with this wonderful, amazing crew.
Life is a journey.
It takes many turns, and I'm just grateful to be here."
For Crew-11 pilot Mike Fincke, it will be his fourth trip to the space station.
His first two flights in 2004 and 2008 were aboard Russia's Soyuz capsule.
In 2011, he flew to the station on Space Shuttle Endeavour — the [last launch of that vehicle](https://www.npr.org/2011/05/16/136353810/shuttle-endeavour-blasts-off-on-final-mission).
### [Space](https://www.npr.org/sections/space/)
### [Is Trump preparing to cancel America's ride back to the moon?](https://www.npr.org/2025/02/19/g-s1-49451/artemis-moon-nasa-sls-rocket-doge-musk)
There has been a continual human presence on the space station since its first crew arrived on October 31, 2000.
"We have a beautiful space station.

I'm very proud of our space station," said Fincke ahead of his launch. "This is something that I think that humans should just really remember of all the cool things we can do when we work together constructively."
The mission marks the second trip to the station for Japan's Yui Kimiya.

# NASA’s SpaceX Crew-11 Mission Returns, Splashes Down off California
![Profile image for Gerelle Q.
### NASA Headquarters
### Johnson Space Center
![](https://images-assets.nasa.gov/image/KSC-20260428-PH-GEB02_0010/KSC-20260428-PH-GEB02_0010~large.jpg?w=1920&h=1280&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)
### Kennedy Space Center
![](https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/crew-11-in-dragon-jan-15.jpg?w=2048)

NASA’s SpaceX Crew-11 mission safely splashed down early Thursday morning in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, concluding a more than five-month mission aboard the International Space Station.

NASA astronauts [Zena Cardman](https://www.nasa.gov/people/zena-cardman/) and [Mike Fincke](https://www.nasa.gov/people/edward-michael-mike-fincke/), JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) astronaut Kimiya Yui, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Oleg Platonov returned to Earth at 12:41 a.m.
Teams aboard SpaceX recovery vessels retrieved the spacecraft and its crew shortly after landing.

“I couldn’t be prouder of our astronauts and the teams on the ground at NASA, SpaceX, and across our international partnerships,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Their professionalism and focus kept the mission on track, even with an adjusted timeline.
Crew-11 completed more than 140 science experiments that advance human exploration.

Missions like Crew-11 demonstrate the capability inherent in America’s space program—our ability to bring astronauts home as needed, launch new crews quickly, and continue pushing forward on human spaceflight as we prepare for our historic Artemis II mission, from low Earth orbit to the Moon and ultimately Mars.”
Crew-11 returned home about a month earlier than planned because of a medical concern teams are monitoring with one of the crew members, who remains stable.
Due to medical privacy, it is not appropriate for NASA to share more details about the crew member.

Prior to return, NASA [previously coordinated](https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/2026/01/08/nasa-shares-latest-update-on-international-space-station-operations-2/) for all four crew members to be transported to a local hospital for additional evaluation, taking advantage of medical resources on Earth to provide the best care possible.
Following the planned overnight hospital stay, the crew members will return to NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston and undergo standard postflight reconditioning and evaluations.
The Crew-11 mission [lifted off](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasas-spacex-crew-11-launches-to-international-space-station/) at 11:43 a.m.
EDT on Aug.1, 2025, from Launch Complex 39A at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
About 15 hours later, the crew’s SpaceX Dragon spacecraft docked to the orbital outpost at 1:27 a.m.
CDT on Aug. 2.
During their 167-day mission, the four crew members traveled nearly 71 million miles and completed more than 2,670 orbits around Earth.
The Crew-11 mission was Fincke’s fourth spaceflight, Yui’s second, and the first for Cardman and Platonov.
Fincke has logged 549 days in space, ranking him fourth among all NASA astronauts for cumulative days in space.
Along the way, Crew-11 logged hundreds of hours of research, maintenance, and technology demonstrations.
The crew members also celebrated the [25th anniversary](https://www.nasa.gov/international-space-station/iss25/) of continuous human presence aboard the orbiting laboratory on Nov. 2, 2025.
Research conducted aboard the space station advances scientific knowledge and demonstrates new technologies that enable us to prepare for human exploration of the Moon and Mars.

NASA’s Commercial Crew Program provides reliable access to space, maximizing the use of the International Space Station for research and development by partnering with private U.S. companies, including SpaceX, to transport astronauts to and from the space station.
Learn more about NASA’s Commercial Crew Program at:

Johnson Space Center, Houston
Steven Siceloff
Kennedy Space Center, Florida

**By** [Aurielle Eady](https://fox35orlando.com/person/e/aurielle-eady)

![REPLAY: SpaceX's Crew-11 rocket launch from Florida](https://static-media.fox.com/fmcv3/prod/fts/A-189007/3msvq7sid9dg3jkn.jpg)
![REPLAY: SpaceX's Crew-11 rocket launch from Florida](https://static-media.fox.com/fmcv3/prod/fts/A-189007/3msvq7sid9dg3jkn.jpg)
#### [REPLAY: SpaceX's Crew-11 rocket launch from Florida](https://fox35orlando.com/video/1684412)
NASA and SpaceX successfully launched the Crew-11 mission from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Friday, and the spacecraft is now en route to the International Space Station (ISS):
#### The Brief
* + NASA and SpaceX launched the Crew-11 mission from Florida and are headed to the ISS on Friday at 11:43 a.m. EDT.
+ The mission includes astronauts from NASA, JAXA, and Roscosmos for a six-month ISS stay.
+ Crew-11 supports long-duration spaceflight and research as part of NASA’s Commercial Crew Program.

**CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla.** - NASA and SpaceX successfully launched the Crew-11 mission from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Friday, and the spacecraft is now en route to the International Space Station (ISS).

The four-person crew—NASA astronauts Zena Cardman and Mike Fincke, Kimiya Yui of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), and Oleg Platonov of Roscosmos—boarded SpaceX’s Dragon spacecraft ahead of liftoff on a Falcon 9 rocket at 11:43 a.m.
EDT.
FOX 35 News is streaming live coverage of the rocket launch in the video player above.

***Stay tuned below for real-time updates throughout the event:***
## Crew-11 astronauts launch on Falcon 9 rocket from Florida
**11:43 a.m. |** SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket has lifted off carrying four Crew-11 astronauts to the International Space Station.
## **Dragon spacecraft is a 'go’ for launch; Falcon 9 fueling underway**
**11: 17 a.m. |** The Dragon crew spacecraft is ready for NASA’s SpaceX Crew-11 launch, with Falcon 9 fueling already started and second stage fueling beginning soon.

**11:11 a.m. |** The crew access arm has been pulled back, and soon the Dragon spacecraft’s emergency escape system will be turned on. This system lets the NASA SpaceX Crew-11 astronauts safely get away if something goes wrong from the time the Falcon 9 rocket takes off until they reach space, which takes about 12 minutes. After that, they will start loading fuel into the rocket.
## **Crew-11 astronauts arrive at launch site at the Kennedy Space Center**
**9:58 a.m.|** With communication checks finished, the hatch on the SpaceX Dragon spacecraft is now sealed.
9 a.m. | Crew-11 astronauts have arrived at the launch site and have boarded the SpaceX Dragon spacecraft.
**8:33 a.m. |** The likelihood of favorable launch weather has dropped from 75% to 60%, according to SpaceX.
8:20 a.m. | The Crew-11 astronauts have suited up and are headed to Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center.
**8:13 a.m. |** Officials will hold a brief meeting at 9:43 a.m. to discuss any potential weather concerns ahead of liftoff.
**7:54 a.m. |** The astronauts are suiting up in the Astronaut Crew Quarters inside the Neil A. Armstrong Operations and Checkout Building at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
## Crew-11 launch time
Timeline:
Liftoff is set for 11:43 a.m.
EDT from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
A backup opportunity is available on Saturday.

The launch was originally planned for Thursday afternoon but [was called off](https://www.fox35orlando.com/news/crew-11-rocket-launch-today-from-florida) T-minus one minute before liftoff due to cloud cover, violating weather safety criteria.
## What is the weather forecast for the Crew-11 launch?
What we know:
The likelihood of favorable launch weather has dropped from 75% to 60%, according to SpaceX.
FOX 35 Storm Team Meteorologist Jessica Dobson said as the sea-breeze begins to kick in and move inland, it typically helps produce clouds initially and eventually showers/storms.
The exact placement of the clouds will be crucial for the launch, and it won't be an entirely cloudy or overcast sky.
## What is the purpose of the Crew-11 mission?
Big picture view:
Once aboard the ISS, the team will spend about six months conducting scientific experiments, running technology demos, and preparing for future exploration — including the Moon and beyond.
Their work supports both life on Earth and future human missions into deep space.
The mission will mark the next exciting chapter in NASA and SpaceX's partnership to support long-duration human spaceflight and cutting-edge research in low-Earth orbit.

Crew-11 is the 11th crew rotation mission of SpaceX's human space transportation system and its 12th flight with astronauts, including the Demo-2 test flight, to the space station through NASA's Commercial Crew Program.
**The Source:** This story was written based on information shared by NASA and SpaceX.

**SpaceX Crew-11** was the eleventh operational NASA [Commercial Crew Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_Crew_Program "Commercial Crew Program") flight and the 19th crewed orbital flight of a [Crew Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crew_Dragon "Crew Dragon") spacecraft. The mission transported four crew members, [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") astronauts [Zena Cardman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zena_Cardman "Zena Cardman") and [Michael Fincke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Fincke "Michael Fincke"), [JAXA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JAXA "JAXA") astronaut [Kimiya Yui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimiya_Yui "Kimiya Yui"), and [Roscosmos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roscosmos "Roscosmos") cosmonaut [Oleg Platonov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleg_Platonov_(cosmonaut) "Oleg Platonov (cosmonaut)"), to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") (ISS). The mission launched on August 1, 2025 and docked with the ISS the next day. On January 8, 2026, NASA announced that the mission would end about a month earlier than planned due to a medical situation involving Fincke.
